claims.claim: Arendt divides human realms, actions, and types of humans into three categories ordered by value and authenticity, with the private realm at the lowest level and the public realm as the highest.

claims.claim: For Arendt, the public realm consists of two distinct yet interrelated dimensions: the space of appearance and the shared common world.
claims.supporting_excerpt: نظر آرنت قلمرو عمومی از دو بعد     فضای آزادی ؛ فضای نمود است ، اولی. شود حال مرتبط به هم تشکیل می درعينمتمایز و از طریق سخن و اقناع ، صورت هماهنگ و جمعی و برابری سیاسی که هرگاه شهروندان به جهان مشترک و عمومیِ    ؛ است  جهان مشترک ، دومی. آید به وجود می، کنند عمل می

definitions.definition: The highest realm for Arendt, which is the locus of citizens who are actors and involves both the space of appearance and the common world.

distinctions.distinction: The private realm is the lowest hierarchical order associated with labor and mere behavior, whereas the public realm is the highest order associated with action, speech, and the space of appearance.

must_not_be_lost: Arendt's three-part division of realms (private vs. public)
The two dimensions of the public realm: space of appearance and shared common world
